findings.summary: The caption's hook is a misleading clickbait question about bombing an interview, and the caption never says what sharding teaches.
findings.evidence: "Bombed a system design interview on databases? Part 2 of 10 DATABASE CONCEPTS YOU CAN'T SKIP IN SYSTEM DESIGN INTERVIEWS covers 10. Sharding."
findings.fix: Open with a concrete hook about the content, e.g. "One bad shard key can melt your database — here's how to pick one and reshard safely." Then name the series and part.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY callout sits in the middle of the page and refers to resharding and cross-shard queries before the RESHARDING section and the fan-out code example have been taught.
findings.evidence: The callout "Be ready to discuss resharding and cross-shard queries." comes before the "RESHARDING" heading, the numbered resharding steps and the "No shard key means fan-out" code block.
findings.fix: Move the takeaway callout to the end of the page, after the code block and the "Exhaust first" tip, so the page closes with the summary.

findings.summary: The caption includes the raw list number "10." and calls this "Part 2 of 10", which conflicts with the series numbering, where 10 is the concept count and this part covers only the last concept.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of 10 DATABASE CONCEPTS ... covers 10. Sharding." and series "...PART 2"
findings.fix: Drop the "10." prefix and reword, e.g. "Part 2 of the series: Sharding." Do not read "Part 2 of 10" as 10 parts.

findings.summary: The hashtags include irrelevant or off-topic tags for sharding content.
findings.fix: Remove #sql and #learntocode, since sharding is not SQL-specific or beginner coding. Add relevant tags such as #sharding, #distributedsystems, #scalability.

findings.summary: The tip to put the shard key in every query is separated from the code that demonstrates it, with the resharding section in between.
findings.evidence: The tip "Put the shard key in every query and every primary key so the router hits one shard." appears early. The supporting example, "-- user_id in every query: 1 shard ... -- no user_id: scatter to all 4", comes only after the RESHARDING bullets.
findings.fix: Put the code block directly after the shard-key tip, then start RESHARDING.
